One branch of a hyperbola (shown above) is defined by the parametric equations

$$
x=3\operatorname{tan}⁡t,\,y=6\operatorname{sec}⁡t.
$$

What is the domain of the parameter $t?$

The quarter-hyperbola above is defined by the parametric equations

$$
x=5\operatorname{tan}⁡t,\,y=\sqrt{6}\operatorname{sec}⁡t.
$$

Determine the domain of the parameter $t$ for this quarter, assuming that the entire hyperbola is defined only for $t\in [-\pi ,\pi ].$

feedback.worked_solution:
The parametric equations of the full hyperbola are

$$
x=5\operatorname{tan}⁡t,\,y=\sqrt{6}\operatorname{sec}⁡t,\,t\in [-\pi ,\pi ],\,t\ne \pm \frac{\pi }{2}.
$$

To restrict the parameterization to a quarter-hyperbola, we refer to the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14093765/assets/f5b8c47a703f86efb82cbc7efb8713738799304484f3a325da17b48b03459340.png)

We can see that if we restrict $t$ to $(\frac{\pi }{2},\pi ]$ we get the required quarter-hyperbola.

Therefore, the parametric equations that describe the required quarter-hyperbola are

$$
x=5\operatorname{tan}⁡t,\,y=\sqrt{6}\operatorname{sec}⁡t,\,t\in (\frac{\pi }{2},\pi ].
$$
